title: Infrastructure Lab Technician Apprentice
description: At IBM Infrastructure & Technology, we design and operate the systems that keep the world running. From high-resiliency mainframes and hybrid cloud platforms to networking, automation, and site reliability. Our teams ensure the performance, security, and scalability that clients and industries depend on every day. Working in Infrastructure & Technology means tackling complex challenges with curiosity and collaboration. You'll work with diverse technologies and colleagues worldwide to deliver resilient, future-ready solutions that power innovation. With continuous learning, career growth, and a supportive culture, IBM provides the opportunities to build expertise and shape the infrastructure that drives progress. As an Infrastructure Lab Technician Apprentice at IBM, you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge and experience using the latest tools and technologies to support IBM processors, storage or other semiconductor hardware. Throughout your apprenticeship, you will work closely with experienced engineers, technicians and other mentors in a production and/or development hardware raised floor environment to maintain all specific hardware related to the IBM Infrastructure Group. Where applicable, you will be taught all day-to-day activities/responsibilities of a hardware raised floor environment on multiple different Infrastructure specific raised floors. This work will be physical hands on in nature with some lifting and physical dexterity requirements. You will also learn and be responsible for a variety of lab safety procedures relevant to the specific raised floor environment, as well as learning and utilizing the specific hardware life cycle workload applications. To that end, you will be trained and expected to certify via testing in all specific responsibilities. Specific to the hardware life cycle, you will be expected to rack, stack, cable (power and network), new hardware, as well as un-rack and pack old hardware and cabling. What is an Apprenticeship? IBM Apprenticeship Program is an official registered apprenticeship recognized by the Department of Labor (DOL). Every graduate of a Registered Apprenticeship program receives a nationally recognized credential from the DOL. During the apprenticeship duration, you will be required to complete specific learning hours and on the job training that has been outlined to ensure you are developing the skills and competencies essential to the role. You will be able to learn and grow at your own pace, but we expect most apprentices will complete their learning within 12 months. Once you graduate and receive your certificate from our apprentice program, you will be eligible to apply to available full-time roles at IBM. Who you are An apprenticeship is about learning. We’re seeking candidates who have the following requirements, but we know you’re just getting your career started, and we’re committed to helping you learn and grow. If you’ve had some experience with data analysis or simply working in a team oriented environment in the past, you’re exactly the type of candidate we’re looking for. To be successful, you need: Drive and eagerness to learn Ability to work independently, and in an efficient and organized manner Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team Strong troubleshooting Some basic knowledge or experience in electrical engineering sciences i.e. Electrical Safety, Electron Theory, AC/DC Basics, Wires and Cables, Computer Electronics, Electrical Testing Equipment What’s the experience? As an apprentice, you'll join with other apprentices in a local cohort. You'll go through your first few weeks together, learning about IBM and the skills you'll be attaining throughout your apprenticeship. Then, you'll work with your managers and mentors to progress through your personal skills roadmap, learning and demonstrating new knowledge and competencies through hands-on application with your project teams. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Relocation assistance is not available. Willingness to complete the requirements of the apprenticeship program High School Diploma or GED Some knowledge or experience with any of the following: Physical computer hardware installation Workstation problem and change tools for workload tracking, PC based Must be able to team lift large hardware units Must be able to work in fast paced physically demanding environment Preferred Technical and Professional Experience - None Required Education - High School Diploma/GED Preferred Education - Associate's Degree/College Diploma United States Infrastructure & Technology Internship Austin, US Austin (0147) International Business Machines Corporation Computer Hardware Installation Education Infrastructure Hardware Professionalism

title: Staff Software Engineer, Internal Products
location: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As Anthropic grows, more of the work our own teams do every day runs through internal software, and that software has to keep up. We are building that software, and we are building it Claude-first: Claude should take on as much of the repetitive, multi-step work as it safely can, and people decide what needs a human. We’re looking for Staff+ full-stack engineers to drive this work. You’ll build across the stack: the products people use and the agents that work alongside them. You’ll work directly with the teams who rely on what you build. Many of these workflows write to business-critical data, so correctness matters as much as speed. This is a greenfield opportunity: you’ll shape the underlying systems, ship agents that take real work off people’s plates, and design how people and agents get the right context to make good decisions. Key responsibilities Design and ship internal products end to end, from the data model to the UI, for workflows that teams across Anthropic depend on. Put Claude to work on real tasks, such as gathering the context a decision needs, drafting the next step of a multi-step process or keeping records consistent across the systems teams already use, and decide where an agent should act and where a well-designed UI is the better answer. Make agents safe to trust with real work: scoped access to data, guardrails, evals, audit trails, and clear points where a person confirms before anything happens. Build one set of shared capabilities that people and agents both use, exposed as APIs and MCP tools, so the same rules and approvals apply to whoever makes the call. Treat speed and polish as product requirements. Spend time with the people who use what you build, find where their work slows down, and remove those steps. Build for correctness. When a workflow writes to business-critical data, a mistake travels into other systems, so you’ll know where idempotency, reconciliation and audit trails matter and where they don’t. Integrate with the third-party systems teams already rely on, and build the layer on top of them where people and agents get their work done. Set technical direction for a product area over multiple quarters, lead engineers across teams through large, ambiguous projects, and make the engineers around you better through design reviews, code review and mentorship. Operate what you ship: own the reliability of the workflows people depend on and be on call for them. Minimum qualifications Experience shipping production software as a backend-leaning full-stack engineer, comfortable designing a data model, an API and the UI on top of them. Experience building software on LLMs or agents, and a point of view on when an agent should act on its own and when it should ask first. Experience leading the design and delivery of complex, user-facing products across the full stack, through requirements that shifted while you built. Experience designing for correctness and data integrity from the start, in systems where errors are costly and hard to undo. Experience working closely with non-engineering partners, turning ambiguous needs into clear requirements and reaching decisions together. Preferred qualifications Experience building internal tools or platforms that other teams rely on. A plus, not a requirement; strong product generalists are just as welcome. Experience taking an agent into production for a high-stakes workflow, including the evals and guardrails that made it safe to ship. Experience building a zero-to-one product, or rebuilding one that people already depended on every day. Experience building on top of third-party platforms through their APIs, and knowing when to extend a system and when to build your own. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. title: Applied AI Research Intern - R&D Internship – 2027 - YORKTOWN HEIGHTS
description: Join the pioneering Software Innovation Lab team at IBM Software and contribute to shaping the future foundations of artificial intelligence and data. Our group of applied scientists and software developers is dedicated to conducting end-to-end research that delivers real-world AI impact through a rigorous, responsible, and open innovation framework. We are the R&D team that is the innovation engine of IBM Software, shaping the technologies that IBM customers rely on – today and in the future. As an AI Research Intern, you will explore cutting-edge research areas, with a focus on AI models and approaches for real-time data and context backbone for agents and stream-native AI. Internship topics include event world models, real-time context optimization for agents and models, semantic stream processing for stored and streaming data. You will explore efficiency, accuracy and scalability challenges, test new theories, design experiments to validate novel computational models, all within a collaborative environment that bridges fundamental science and transformative engineering. You will help develop Event World Models, a new class of AI systems that learn, reason, predict, and plan from continuously evolving event streams and enterprise data. You will contribute across the research lifecycle, from formulating research questions and designing novel algorithms to building prototypes and evaluating them through rigorous experimentation. Research topics include event-driven world modeling, temporal and causal reasoning, symbolic and foundation models for structured and streaming data, semantic action discovery, AI agents, and stream-native AI systems capable of real-time prediction, what-if analysis, and decision-making.
